llm.summary: The skill is purpose-aligned for JD logistics lookups, but it handles tokens and user-supplied query values in ways that create serious security review concerns.

dimensions.detail: The scripts read an API token from process.env.token and transmit logistics identifiers, filters, and business metrics to external endpoints; this is purpose-aligned but sensitive and under-disclosed to users.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The README uses mutable global installation commands such as npm i -g clawhub and clawhub install with --force, which is a supply-chain and overwrite risk, but not evidence of malicious behavior in this artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to place user-derived values directly into shell command templates without quoting, including warehouse names and tracking numbers, which creates a realistic command-injection risk if executed through a shell.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no service, scheduler, backdoor, or persistent worker, but the setup advises storing credentials in user-level environment configuration and one README path uses ~/.env, increasing credential exposure risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The package coherently provides logistics tracking and operational indicator queries by running bundled Node.js scripts against JD/Ochama HTTPS APIs; those network calls and token use fit the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only with a narrowly scoped JD logistics token, avoid storing secrets in ~/.env or shared user profiles, and do not run the command templates with raw user input. The TLS bypass and unquoted command instructions should be fixed before production use.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: all three API scripts set rejectUnauthorized: false while sending a token header, so TLS server authentication is disabled for sensitive logistics API requests.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: SKILL.md templates require direct, unquoted substitution of user-derived values into node commands; command execution is expected, but this unsafe construction is not necessary for the purpose.
[PE3] expected: Partly confirmed and downgraded from credential-theft concern: token access is expected for authenticated logistics APIs, but README storage guidance and inconsistent token naming are weak secret-handling practices.
[T08] expected: Confirmed as a supply-chain caution: install instructions use mutable package and skill names and --force, but this is documentation risk rather than artifact-backed malicious behavior.
[LP3] unexpected: Confirmed as an under-disclosure issue: no explicit allowed-tools or permission scope is declared, despite the skill expecting local command execution and network API access.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only documentation and output appear consistent with a JD logistics business workflow; this is a usability/localization limitation, not a security basis for escalation.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed minor quality issues: several parameter and empty-result instructions conflict, which can cause incorrect queries or responses but does not show deception.
